               PUBLIC HEARINGS

               4.1    BYLAW NO. 2044

                      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2044 at 5:35 pm.





Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Kelsey Waller has applied on behalf
of 2621 Sooke Developments Ltd. to amend the zoning of 2621 Sooke Road and 3260
Jacklin Road from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the Residential
Townhouse (RTl) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 92
townhomes.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.   That as a bonus for increased density:

     a.    $2,074 per unit to the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and

     b. $610 per unit to the Affordable Housing Fund.

2. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan and a construction
   parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit;
     and

3. That prior to BylawAdoption, a subdivision plan that includes the required road
     dedication, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood and
Neighbourhood Centre designation.

Notifications and advertiisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

This rezoning should include a covenant that indoor parking spaces will be kept clear of
storage so as to be used for parking.

Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

The applicant. Abstract Developments, gave a presentation on the proposal, outlining
the site characteristics, neighbourhood consultation process, and the project designs.

J. Bradlev, 2638 Alderglen PI. expressed opposition to the proposed project, expressing
concerns about the high level of density and impacts to wildlife.

A. Spargo. 1013 Gala Crt, expressed support for the proposal, noting that it is a good fit
for the area.

B. Cubit. #103-2745 Veterans Memorial Pkwv, expressed support for the proposal.

M. Degagne, 1037 Boxcar Cl. expressed support for the proposal, noting that it would
help first-time homeowners and that the location is fitting for the proposal.

I. Philips. 3509 Mvles Mansell Rd. expressed support for the proposal, noting that the
impacts to current residents would be minimal and that there would be net benefits to
the community.

M. Wagner. #104-2669 Deville Rd. expressed concerns about the density to the area and
would like retention of mature trees.




      T. Baldwin. 2642 Alderglen PI. expressed concerns about the proposed density.
      L. Webb. 2669 Mill Pond Ter. expressed support for the proposal and the additional
      housing that it would create.

      I. Davkin. 2618 Ernhill Drive, expressed concerns about the proposed density and innpact
      to trees.


      S. Koloiian, 896 Rowils Cr. expressed support for the proposal.

      N. Everett. 2611 Sooke Rd. expressed concerns about the proposed density.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations.

      R. Larose. 3260 Jacklin Rd. expressed support for the proposal.

      The Mayor declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2044 closed at 6:12 pm.
      Mayor Young left the meeting at 6:15 pm. due to a perceived conflict with Item 4.2.

4.2   BYLAW NO. 2052

      Acting Mayor Wade opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No.2052 at 6:13 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Chad Bryden has applied on behalf
      of Darlene & David Smith, Limona Construction Ltd, Thomas Gruber, and Carol &
      Andrew Mack to amend the zoning of 829, 831, 835, and 839 Hockley Avenue from the
      R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone and RM3 (Apartment) Zone to the CCl (City
      Centre) Zone.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of two six-storey
      apartment buildings.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
      bonus for increased density:

      1. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
      2. $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund,

      Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
      Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy

      3. That the applicant also agrees to provide, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219
         covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the
         following:

          a.   That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan and a
               construction parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000
               standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance
               of a Building Permit;





    b. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades required
         to the services and utilities required for the development;

    c. That no occupancy permits shall be issued until the roundabout at Peatt Road,
       and Hockley Avenue has been completed and is operational, to the satisfaction
         of the Director oif Engineering;

    d. That the building be strata titled into individual residential units prior to the
       issuance of an occupancy permit, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;

    e. That the developer consolidate the parcels into a minimum of two lots in
       accordance with the CCl zone regulations, prior to the issuance of a
         development permit;

    f.   That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for
         the proposed residential building(s) that ensures parking is allocated to each
         unit and visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in
         exchange for compensation separate from that of a residential unit; and
    g. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parkingspaces, shall
       feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to
         the parking space; and

         1. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
         2. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load
            sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance
             standard to ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and

         3. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment
            (EVSE) in operation and the Strata Council may not prevent an owner,
            occupant, or tenant from installing the EV charging equipment.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

Acting Mayor Wade called a first time for presentations.

The applicant gave a presentation on the proposal, providing an overview of the project
components, design, and location.

S. O'Sullivan. 821 Hocklev Ave. expressed concerns about parking and potential impacts
to trees.


Acting Mayor Wade called a second time for presentations.

R. Stoerzer. #7-848 Hocklev Ave, expressed concerns about traffic, parking, and
pedestrian safety.

M. Wagner. #104-2669 Deville Rd, expressed concerns about the lack of proposed green
space.





             Acting IVIayor Wade called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none,
             he declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2052 closed at 6:31 pm.

             Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 6:34 pm.

candidates.raw_motion_text:
THAT Committee of the Whole receive this report for information;
               AND
               THAT the Committee recommend that:
               1. Council directs staff to prepare a Standing Internal Borrowing Governance Bylaw for
               Council's consideration, establishing the following minimum requirements for all future
               interfund borrowing under Community Charter:
                       a. The term of any internal loan.
                       b. A formal Internal Loan Agreement.
                       c. The Interest calculated using a publicly defined methodology.
                       d. The specific Internal Loan Agreement and its repayment schedule to be
                       attached as a schedule or appendix to the annual Five-Year Financial Plan Bylaw.
               2. Council directs staff to prepare a Remediation Plan for all internal debt balances
               outstanding as of December 31, 2025, and present this Plan to Council in advance of the
               2027 Financial plan. The Remediation Plan shall include at a minimum:

      Calculate the total accrued foregone interest on all existing internal debt.
      Establish a repayment schedule for all principal and accrued interest, with a specified
      repayment period.
      Identify the proposed funding source for the required interest and principal repayments;
      AND
      3. Council directs staff to amend all relevant policies, to align fully with the requirements
      of the new Internal Borrowing Governance Bylaw once adopted.

            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 514, (2844 Millstream Rd), 2017".


The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1748 at 5:32 p.m.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or
her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after

                                                                                                      January 8th, 2018
                                                                                                           Page 2 of 16


everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Pascal Toupin- Selinger with Ironclad Developments has applied on behalf
of Andre Louis Cottyn to amend the zoning of 2844 Millstream Rd from the CS1 (Service Commercial) Zone
to the MUlA (Mixed Use Residential Commercial A) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to include the subject parcel in plans to construct an apartment building
on 720, 724 and 732 Meaford Avenue.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:


1.   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
     unit, which may be reduced by 75% if rental tenure is secured for a term of no less than 10 years, prior
     to subdivision approval:


     a)     $2,562 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
     b)     $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all
other charges on title, that agrees to the following:


           i.That the applicant provide a construction parking management plan, to the satisfaction of the
              Director of Engineering, prior to issuance of a building permit;
           ii.That the applicant provide a stormwater management plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
              Engineering and in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000, prior to subdivision approval or building
              permit issuance, whichever is first;
          iii.That the applicant acknowledges and agrees to design the proposed development, in accordance
              to the updated parking regulations as determined by Council, to the discretion of the Director of
              Planning;
          iv.That the applicant agrees to implement the approved storm water management plan and to
              complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to on site and off site infrastructure
          necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject property at the applicant's expense;
       v.That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements, including, but not limited to, the
          installation of a sidewalk to the corner of Meaford and Millstream Road to align with the sidewalk
          infrastructure required along Meaford Road, in accordance with Bylaw No.1000 and to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to subdivision approval or building permit
          issuance, whichever is first;
      vi.That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or
          other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled at the applicant's expense; and
      vii.That the applicant acknowledges the proximity to industrial business operators may be a nuisance
          to the future residents of the development;


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 516, (798 Goldstream Ave; 2747, 2753, 2761, 2769

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1750 at 5:34 p.m.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his
or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after
everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Niall Paltiel of Island View Strategies has applied on behalf of Bishop of
Victoria Corporation (Our Lady of Rosary Catholic Church) to amend the zoning of 2747, 2753, 2761, 2769,
and 2779 Peatt Road; 2734, 2738, 2742, 2746, 2750, and 2756 Claude Road; and 798 Goldstream Avenue
from the P2 (Community Institutional), R1 (One-Family Residential), R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential)
Zone to a new C9 (Community Town Centre Pedestrian 9) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for a future mixed-used development on these properties
along with a new church and parish location.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.
     a.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:
                i.     $1,525 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                       $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund.

which case the applicant may request that Council amend Bylaw No. 1750 to include the contribution
amounts.

     b.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           square metre of commercial space, prior to issuance of a building permit:
                i.   $10.75 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.


     c.    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the following:
                i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                      managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director
                      of Engineering.
                      The registration of a lot consolidation plan that includes road dedication along Peatt
                      Road, Goldstream Avenue, and Claude Road to the satisfaction of the Manager of
                      Land Development and Director of Engineering;
                      The registration a blanket statutory right of way on the proposed church/assisted
                      living site for a pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road; and
               iv.    The registration of a blanket statutory right of way on the southwest site for the
                      future installation of a pedestrian friendly plaza in the southwest corner, which would
                      include art work.
     d.   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority
          of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
                 i.   That a 2.0m wide pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road be
                      constructed with red brick paves and lighting prior to issuance of a building permit,

                      That the southwest corner of the proposed commercial/residential site have a 300m2

                      That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed to the satisfaction of the

              a.   That the following contributions are included in the bylaw as an amenity for increased

                     ii.   $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.

                 includes the following:
                     i.  The owner pay for and construct all works to restrict left turn movements
                         southbound on Claude Road to Goldstream Avenue prior to issuance of

                    ii.  The owner provide a traffic and public safety plan and construction parking
                         management plan, prior to any onsite works and/or clearing, to the
                         satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

                         the standards of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 and

                         maintenance prior to the request for Occupancy Permit as a condition of
                         rezoning.

     to the applicant paying the City $5,000 for the one deficient stall prior to issuance of a building
     permit.

candidates.raw_motion_text:
That Council:

1.   Give First Reading to Bylaw No. 1673 to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 616
     Goldstream Ave from RM2 to RM7A, subject to the following terms and conditions:

             a) That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
                 in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                     i.     That a stormwater maintenance covenant be registered on title prior to the request
                            for Occupancy Permit as a condition of rezoning;
                    ii.     That the owner provide a construction parking management plan to the satisfaction
                            of the Director of Engineering prior to the commencement of any works on-site;
                    iii.    That the owner will provide a new queue length assessment from a traffic engineer
                            to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building
                            Permit for Building 2;

                                                                            Regular Council Agenda — March 6th, 2017
                                                                                                       Page 6 of 12



   2.   Provide a permissive tax exemption, on land and improvements, subject to a covenant being
        registered on title that the proposed residential units will be non-profit affordable housing rental
        units for at least 10 years;

   3.   Authorize the Director of Planning to issue a variance to the required off-street parking for
        Building 1 with a condition that the amount of parking provided for Building 1 be reassessed prior
        to the commencement of Phase 2, and that additional parking spaces be allocated to users of
        Building 1 if the amount of parking is deemed insufficient at that time;


   4.   Direct staff to proceed with the proposed design of Building 1 through the development permit
        process.

   5.   Waive all required amenity contributions and application fees charged by the City of Langford to
        allow the 160-unit subsidized affordable housing rental development proposed in this application
        subject to the owner registering a Section 219 Covenant requiring the new residential units will
        be subsidized non-profit affordable housing rental units for at least 10 years AND direct staff to
        amend the Amenity Contribution Policy and any necessary development application fee bylaws
        to waive the required amenity contributions and application fees for any subsequent subsidized
        affordable housing rental development.

              a.   That the following contributions are included in the bylaw as an amenity for increased

That Council:

1.   Give First Reading to Bylaw No. 1673 to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 616
     Goldstream Ave from RM2 to RM7A, subject to the following terms and conditions:

             a) That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
                 in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                     i.     That a stormwater maintenance covenant be registered on title prior to the request
                            for Occupancy Permit as a condition of rezoning;
                    ii.     That the owner provide a construction parking management plan to the satisfaction
                            of the Director of Engineering prior to the commencement of any works on-site;
                    iii.    That the owner will provide a new queue length assessment from a traffic engineer
                            to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building
                            Permit for Building 2;

                                                                            Regular Council Agenda — March 6th, 2017
                                                                                                       Page 6 of 12



   2.   Provide a permissive tax exemption, on land and improvements, subject to a covenant being
        registered on title that the proposed residential units will be non-profit affordable housing rental
        units for at least 10 years;

   3.   Authorize the Director of Planning to issue a variance to the required off-street parking for
        Building 1 with a condition that the amount of parking provided for Building 1 be reassessed prior
        to the commencement of Phase 2, and that additional parking spaces be allocated to users of
        Building 1 if the amount of parking is deemed insufficient at that time;


   4.   Direct staff to proceed with the proposed design of Building 1 through the development permit
        process.

   5.   Waive all required amenity contributions and application fees charged by the City of Langford to
        allow the 160-unit subsidized affordable housing rental development proposed in this application
        subject to the owner registering a Section 219 Covenant requiring the new residential units will
        be subsidized non-profit affordable housing rental units for at least 10 years AND direct staff to
        amend the Amenity Contribution Policy and any necessary development application fee bylaws
        to waive the required amenity contributions and application fees for any subsequent subsidized
        affordable housing rental development.

That Council


       1. Proceed with consideration of Bylaw No. 1952 to amend the zoning designation of the
          properties located at 753 and 761 Station Avenue from the C3 (District Commercial) and RM7
          (Medium-Density Apartment) zones to the CCl (City Centre) zone subject to the following
          terms and conditions:


                   a)   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                           contributions per dwelling unit, prior to issuance of a Building Permit:
                           i.      $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
                           ii.     $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund

                   subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the Affordable
                   Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

                   b)   That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:
                           i.      A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be
                                   adequately managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the
                                   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

                                                                                               February 16, 2021
                                                                                                    Page 7 of 28


        c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
             registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees:
                i.       That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000
                standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of
                a building permit:
                        a.      Full frontage improvements, including 90-degree parking stalls on
                                Aprell Place, if feasible;
                        b.      A storm water management plan; and
                        c.      A construction parking management plan.
                ii.    That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
                       feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to
                       the parking space, and that
                          a.       Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle
                                   charging;
                          b.       Where an electric vehicle energy management system is
                                   implemented (load sharing), a qualified professional may specify a
                                   minimum performance standard to ensure a sufficient rate of
                                   electric vehicle charging; and
                          c.       The owner/tenant is required to keep the Electric Vehicle
                                   Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in operation and the Strata
                                   Council/landlord may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant
                                   from installing the EV charging equipment
                iii.      That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building
                          permit that prohibits a private or public event, ceremony, function, or the
                          like from occurring in the Banquet Facility and the Legion Hall at the same
                          time, to the satisfaction of the City's Chief Administrative Officer; AND

2. Waive all required amenity contributions for the 65-unit subsidized affordable housing rental
   development proposed with this application subject to the owner registering a section 219
   covenant on title requiring the residential units be subsidized non-profit affordable housing
   units for at least 10-years; AND

3. Replace Section 6.57.08(3) with the following:
   "Surface parking stalls may be located adjacent to an interior side or rear lot line when
   screened by a fence no less than 1.8m (6.0 ft) in height and by a landscaping strip no less than
   1.0m (3.3 ft) in width."; AND

4. Add the following to Appendix J, as section 2.1(g):
   'The Director of Planning may approve development permits with variances to landscaping
   requirements where the design intent of these guidelines and the zone are met"; AND

5. Authorize the Director of Planning it issue the following variances in the Form and Character
   Development Permit for 753 and 761 Station Avenue:
        a)      That Table 1 of Section 4.01.01 be varied to reduce the number of onsite parking
                stalls from the required 214 to 148;
        b)      That Section 6.57.06(l)(b) be varied to reduce the minimum interior side yard
                setback from the required 3.0m to 2.2m;

                                                                                                        February 16, 2021
                                                                                                             Page 8 of 28


                    c)     That Section 6.57.06(2)(a) be varied to reduce the minimum front lot line setback
                           from the required 4.0m to 2.7m.

unresolved.original_motion_text: THAT Council consider bringing forward Bylaw No. 2234 for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd readings to amend the text of Area B of the MUE1 Zone subject to specified terms and conditions (including registration of Section 219 covenant, mitigation and construction parking plans, stormwater management, landscape and habitat restoration plans, low carbon concrete verification, completion of a signalized intersection, and protection of eagle trees/habitat).

candidates.raw_motion_text:
THAT Council:

    1. Consider bringing forward Bylaw No. 2234 for 1st 2nd, and 3rd readings
       at a future Council meeting in order to amend the text of Area B of the
       MUE1 Zone subject to the following terms and conditions:

        a.   That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section 219
             covenant in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the
             following:

             i.    That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw
                   No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
                   Engineering prior to any land alteration:

                   1. A Mitigation Plan; and

                   2. A Construction Parking and Delivery Management Plan.

             ii.   That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw
                   No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
                   Engineering prior to the issuance of a building permit:

                   1.   A Stormwater Management Plan.

             iii. That prior to the issuance of a building permit, the applicant
                  provides a Landscape Plan prepared by a Landscape Architect
                  and signed off by a Registered Professional Biologist confirming
                  habitat restoration objectives are met by the plan, to the
                  satisfaction of the Director of Development Services. At the
                  time of Building Permit, the applicant must provide a landscape
                  bond in accordance with an approved cost estimate prepared by
                  the Landscape Architect, to be returned to the applicant upon
                  completion of the works. Prior to issuance of a building permit,
                  the applicant provides a site lighting plan that complies with the
                  City's design guidelines.

             iv. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete
                 that meets or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming
                 Potential targets based on Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix
                 data, and that prior to the issuance of a Building Permit the
                 applicant shall provide a Type Ill Environmental Product
                 Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global
                 Warming Potential value and confirming that the proposed
                 development meets the requirements of Low Carbon Concrete
                 Policy POL-0167-PLAN;

             v.    That prior to the issuance of an Occupancy Permit, the
                   signalized intersection at Leigh Road and Mantle Heights must
                   be completed, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

             vi. That prior to subdivision approval, a 5.219 covenant be
                 registered in priority of all charges on title to protect identified

                                     eagle trees and associated habitat protection buffer as a non
                                     disturbance area to the satisfaction of the Director of
                                     Development Services.

unresolved.original_motion_text: THAT Temporary Use Permit No. TUP25-0001 is issued by the Council for the City of Langford to Clarity Cannabis BC Ltd. to operate a non-medical cannabis retail store at 105-693 Hoffman Avenue in accordance with the terms and conditions listed and that the permit expire August 19, 2028.

candidates.raw_motion_text:
THAT Temporary Use Permit No. TUP25-0001 is issued by the Council for the City of
            Langford to Clarity Cannabis BC Ltd. to operate a non-medical cannabis retail store on
            the property legally described as Lot A, Section 72, Esquimalt District, Plan VIP72210,
            PID No. 025-111-949 (105-693 Hoffman Avenue), in accordance with Section 493 of the
            Local Government Act, subject to the following terms and conditions, and
            notwithstanding Sec. 3.02.02(5) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300:
            1. Conditions
            a) Exterior walls shall be treated in a manner and colour that is consistent with other
            parts of the building which the business occupies. If the non-medical cannabis retail
            store occupies a standalone building, then the exterior of the building will exhibit
            colours from a muted, earth tone palette with contrasting accent colours for windows,
            trim and doors. Bold or vivid colours that are intended to be distinctive and eye-catching
            (e.g.: lime green or fire engine red) may be used on signage, but not on the building
            facade or trim to the satisfaction of the Director of Development Services;
            b) All windows shall be opaque or constructed with spandrel panels behind. Windows
            and spandrels may not be embellished with any form of imagery;
            c)Security devices, such as window bars or roll shutters, shall be deployed on the inside
            of doors or windows so as to be unobtrusive and invisible from the street;
            d) The applicant shall provide security measures associated with the premises from
            which the non-medical cannabis retail store will operate in accordance with the
            applicant's proposal in response to the City of Langford Request for Proposal for the
           Retail Sales of Cannabis and Cannabis Related Products (RFP), as determined by the
           Chief Administrative Officer;
           e) The applicant shall address issues of nuisance with respect to odours, smoke and
           noise relating to public use of cannabis and cannabis products in accordance with the
           applicant's proposal in response to the RFP and the regulations, terms and conditions
           outlined in the Cannabis Control and Licencing Act of B.C.;
           f) The applicant shall address impairment issues relating to public use of cannabis and
           cannabis products for non-medical purposes in accordance with the applicant's proposal
           in response to the RFP and the regulations, terms and conditions outlined in the
           Cannabis Control and Licencing Act of B.C.;
           g) The non-medical cannabis retail store must be a stand-alone business;
           h) The hours of operation of the non-medical cannabis retail store shall be limited to
           9am to 9pm Sunday through Wednesday and 9am to 10pm Thursday through Saturday;

 i) The applicant shall provide educational initiatives and materials associated with the
impacts and related social concerns of the non-medical use of cannabis and cannabis
 products in accordance with the applicant's proposal in response to the RFP and as
outlined in the Cannabis Retail Store Terms and Conditions, a handbook for the sale of
non-medical cannabis in British Columbia;
j) The applicant shall conform to the regulations stipulated in the Cannabis Control and
Licencing Act of British Columbia B.C. Reg.202/2018;
 k) The Applicant shall ensure that the non-medical cannabis retail sale is in compliance
 with all applicable laws, including all City bylaws;
SIGNAGE
I) All signage shall be subject to a subsequent Sign Development Permit application
process and shall be constructed and placed in accordance with Langford Sign Bylaw
No.1250 and to the satisfaction of the Director of Development Services;
m) All signage shall be architecturally compatible with the style, composition, materials,
colours, and details of the buildings within the development;
n) The location and size of signs shall be architecturally integrated with the overall
design of the buildings;
o) As a condition of issuance of this permit, and notwithstanding what is permitted by
Bylaw No. 1250, the business is limited to three signs only. This signage shall indicate the
name of the business only, and shall not display company slogans, and may not employ
any play on words with respect to cannabis or drug culture. This signage may be
internally illuminated in accordance with City guidelines, but may not be animated in
any way or have variable messaging;
p) Notwithstanding article o), the business may have one illuminated sign which
indicates that the business is open, provided that this signage is affixed to the interior of
a door or window visible from the street and does not exceed an area of 0.2m2 (2ft2);
q) Sandwich board type signs are prohibited;
If a previous Development Permit has been issued with respect to Form and Character
and no new buildings or exterior renovations are being proposed some of these
conditions may be waived.

2. Whereas
a) The non-medicinal use of cannabis and cannabis related products has historically
been prohibited by federal law in Canada and, as a result, has historically been
prohibited by the City under its Zoning Bylaw No. 300;
b) On October 17, 2018, the Federal Government legalized the non-medicinal use of
cannabis and cannabis products;
c) The Federal Government and the Provincial Government have developed a regulatory
framework for the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use;
d) The City wishes to authorize the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products within
its boundaries, but recognizes that there are challenges associated with it doing so;
e) The City issued the Request for Proposals for the Retail Sales of Cannabis and
Cannabis Related Products to seek proposals from individuals and organizations
interested in undertaking the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-
medicinal use within the City's boundaries, and required that proposals include details
as to how the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products would be
addressed;
f) The City received and reviewed over 30 proposals in response to the Request for

             Proposals, and identified Clarity Cannabis BC Ltd.'s proposal as one that best addressed
             the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products; and,
             g) Clarity Cannabis BC Ltd. is committed to assisting the City and taking positive steps to
             address the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products.
             Now therefore be it resolved that Council issue Temporary Use Permit TUP25-0001 to
             Clarity Cannabis BC Ltd. for it to operate a Cannabis Retail Store at 105-693 Hoffman
             Avenue for a three year term subject to the terms and conditions listed within.
             3. Expiry
             THAT the Temporary Use Permit be issued for a period of 36 months and will expire on
             August 19, 2028.

candidates.raw_motion_text:
That Temporary Use Permit No. TUP19-0002 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford to The
Original Farm Langford Ltd. for it to operate a Cannabis Retail Store at 105 & 111- 945 Reunion Avenue
subject to the following terms and conditions:

1.   Whereas:


     A. The non-medicinal use of cannabis and cannabis related products has historically been prohibited
        by federal law/ in Canada and, as a result, has historically been prohibited by the City under its
        Zoning Bylaw No. 300;
     B. On October 17, 2018, the Federal Government legalized the non-medicinal use of cannabis and
        cannabis products;
     C. The Federal Government and the Provincial Government have developed a regulatory framework
        for the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use;
     D. The City wishes to authorize the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products within its

                                                                                                       May 6^ 2019
                                                                                                         Page 3 of 8


         boundaries, but recognizes that there are challenges associated with it doing so;
     E. The City issued the Request for Proposals for the Retail Sales of Cannabis and Cannabis Related
        Products to seek proposals from individuals and organizations interested in undertaking the retail
        sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use within the City's boundaries, and
         required that proposals include details as to how the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis
         and cannabis products would be addressed;
     F. The City received and reviewed over30 proposals in response to the Request For Proposals, and
         identified The Original Farm Langford Ltd.'s proposal as one that best addressed the challenges
         with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products; and,
     G. The Original Farm Langford Ltd. is committed to assisting the City and taking positive steps to
         address the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products,

        Now therefore be it resolved that Council issue Temporary Use Permit TUP19-0002 to The
        Original Farm Langford Ltd. for it to operate a Cannabis Retail Store at #105 & #111 - 945
        Reunion Avenue subject to the terms and conditions including the stipulations outlined in the
        letter dated March 15, 2019 provided by the land owner/agent of the proposed location,
        ANDTHAT commencement of the TUP be subject to an occupancy permit for Units 105 & 111
        - 945 Reunion Avenue being issued by the City of Langford in the Temporary Use Permit as
        presented.

candidates.raw_motion_text:
That Council:


        Give First Reading to Bylaw No. 1840 and Bylaw No. 1841 to amend the zoning of the property
        located at 4365 West Shore Parkway from the RM2A, RR4 and RR5 Zones to the BP2A Zone, and to
        amend the policy designation within the OCP for the property at 4365 West Shore Parkway from
        the Hillside or Shoreline to the Business or Light Industrial subject to the following:

             a.   That the applicant provides, prior to the scheduling of a Public Hearing for Bylaw Nos. 1840
                  and 1841, a technical Stormwater Management memo to the satisfaction of the Director of
                  Engineering;

                                                                                                         May 6^ 2019
                                                                                                           Page 6 of 8


             b. That the applicant provides, prior to scheduling for the Adoption of Bylaw Nos.1840 and
                1841, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees
                  to the following:


                        i. That the applicant provides, prior to the issuance of a building permit, a
                           construction management plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
                       ii. That the applicant provides, prior to building permit issuance, a stormwater
                            management plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
                       iii. That the applicant agrees to implement the stormwater management plan and to
                            complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to the onsite and offsite
                            infrastructure as is necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject property
                            at the applicant's expense; and
                       iv. That any necessary above ground or underground infrastructure or servicing
                            upgrades extensions or other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled at
                           the applicant's expense;

             c.   That Council direct staff to prepared notices of Council's intention to issue a Development
                  Variance Permit with respect to the subject property and to include:

1.   Variances


     The following regulations of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 are varied under
     Section 498 of the Local Government Act:


     a) That Section 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to
        allow subdivision without connecting to the municipal sanitary sewer system, subject to the
        following conditions:

        That a covenant containing the following be registered on the title of the properties, to the
         satisfaction of the Director of Engineering:

         i. That the applicant design the on-site sewage disposal system to the approval of Island Health
            and to the satisfaction of the Chief Building Inspector prior to building permit; and

     b) That Section 8.1 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to allow
        subdivision without water supply provided by the Cityor CRD Water Service, subject to the following
         conditions:


         That a covenant containing the following be registered on the title of the subject property, to the
         satisfaction of the Director of Engineering:

            I.    That all buildings are to be connected to the City's, CRD Water, or an authorized third party
                  distributer such as Sustainable Services Umited (SSL) water system within six (6) months of
                  such service being extended along the frontage of the subject properties to the satisfaction
                  of the Director of Engineering;
           II.    That the owner agrees to support any future petition to extend a Public Water Service
                  system to the subject properties;

                                                                                                        May 6^ 2019
                                                                                                          Page 7 of 8



         III.     That installation of any on-site plunnbing necessary to allow a Public Water Service system
                  to be connected to each building in accordance with the BC Building Code and/or
                  Subdivision and Servicing Bylaw No. 1000, is completed as part of the works and services
                  installed on the subject properties;
         IV.      That the owner prove that a well water supply for potable water is available and the
                  proposed development meets the requirements ofthe City's Subdivision and Development
                  Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 in respect of domestic water supply to the satisfaction of the
                  Director of Engineering prior to subdivision approval;
         V.       That the owner demonstrate that the water wellsto be used on site will not adversely affect
                  the water supply available to the wells on surrounding properties prior to each subdivision
                   of lands to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;
         VI.      Thateach new building install a firesprinkler systeminaccordance withthe applicable NFPA
                  standard, Building Bylaw No. 1160, and the current BC Building Code to the satisfaction of
                   the Chief Building Inspector;
        VII.       That a fire protection strategy be approved prior to each subdivision of the land to the
                   satisfaction of the Fire Chief and Director of Engineering and be installed prior to the
                   issuance of any Building Permits, including backup generators for any necessary pump
                   systems;
       VIII.       That prior to issuance of each building permit the applicant provide a Fire Underwriters

        subdivision without installing underground electrical and telecommunication.

That Council issue Development Variance Permit No. DVP16-0004 for the City of Langford
      to George Banning on behalf of Ernie Skinner to allow for a two-point turnaround on Winster Road
      instead of a cul-de-sac, a reduction of the on-street parking requirement from 1 space to 0, and a
      reduction of the rear lot line setback from 6 m to 1.5 m for a future lot proposed by subdivision
      at 2639 Millstream Road subject to the following terms and conditions:

      1. Appendix
         The site shall be developed in accordance with the site plan attached (Appendix A).

      2.    Variances
            The following regulations of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 and Subdivision and Development Servicing
            Bylaw No. 1000 are varied under Section 498 of the Local Government Act:

            a)   That Section 6.21.06 (1)(a) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied to reduce the required rear
                 lot line setback from 6 m to 1.5 m;

            b) That Section 4.11.4 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied
               from the required one on-street parking stall provided for every two lots in a residential
               development to nil;

            c)   That Section 4.12 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to
                 allow for a permanent two-point turnaround instead of the required cul de sac.

                                                                                                          Page 4 of 10




      3.    Conditions

            The following requirements are imposed under Section 498 of the Local Government Act:

            a) That the applicant install "No Parking" signage as part of the required frontage
                improvements to ensure the road remains usable for emergency vehicles.

candidates.raw_motion_text:
That Council direct staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the zoning designation of the properties
        located at 2148 and 2150 Millstream Road from R2A (One and Two Family Residential 2) and
        RR4 (Rural Residential 4) zone to RT1 (Residential Townhouse) zone, subject to the following
        terms and conditions:

             b) That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                 contributions per dwelling unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:

                     i.   $3660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                    ii.   $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

        That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in
        priority of all other charges on title that agrees to the following:

                   iii.   That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements as per Bylaw No.
                          1000 to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to subdivision
                          approval or building permit issuance, whichever is first;
                   iv.    That the applicant will submit a stormwater management plan to the satisfaction
                          of the Director of Engineering prior to subdivision approval or building permit
                          issuance, whichever is first;
                    v.    That the applicant will submit a construction parking management plan, to the
                          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to building permit issuance;
                   vi.    That the applicant acknowledge the proximity to Western Speed way and the
                          nuisance this location may cause to future owners of the properties; and
                   vii.   That the applicant submit FUS calculations to the satisfaction of the Director of
                          Engineering prior to subdivision approval or building permit issuance, whichever
                          is first.

             c)   That the applicant registers, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a statutory right of way in order to
                  extend Kingbird and Longspur Drives to the northern boundary of the subject to the
                  satisfaction of the Director of Engineering; and

             d) That the applicant registered, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a road dedication plan to widen
                 Millstream Road to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

candidates.raw_motion_text:
That Council:

   1. Give first reading of Bylaw 1710 as presented to amend the text within Zoning Bylaw No. 300 to
       reduce the amount of required landscaping to 0 m between two parcels zoned for multi-
       residential or mixed use residential commercial development.

   2. Give first reading of Bylaw 1710 as presented to amend the zoning designation of the property
       located at "2839 Jacklin Road, 866, 864 and 862 Orono Avenue from MU1, Mixed Residential
       Commercial 1 zone to MU2, Mixed Residential Commercial 2, subject to the following terms and
       conditions:

            a) That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                contributions per dwelling, prior to subdivision approval or building permit issuance,
                whichever is first, and that these may be further reduced if the terms of Council's policies
                for Contribution fee reductions are met:

                    i.        $1525 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                   ii.        $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Amenity Fund


            b) That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw First Reading, the following:
                  i     A frontage design drawing that identifies all required road dedications, and a left
                         hand turn lane on Orono Avenue into the subject site and a left hand turn lane
                        on Orono Avenue on to Jacklin Road;

            c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

                                                                                              June 19TH, 2017
                                                                                                 Page 6 of 10




                   Confirmation that the applicant has engaged the public regarding the application
                   to rezone the property at 2839 Jacklin Road and 866, 864 and 862 Orono Avenue.

       d) That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
           in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

             i.    That the applicant agrees to provide full frontage improvements to the standards
                   of the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No.1000, and to the
                   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, which will include left turn lanes on
                   Orono Avenue to Jacklin Road and a left turn lane on Orono Avenue to the subject
                   site,
             ii.   That any necessary underground or above ground servicing upgrades, extensions,
                   or other required servicing requirements be fulfilled at the applicant's expense;
            iii.   That prior to the issuance of a building permit, the applicant provides a
                   stormwater management plan to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering
                   and that the applicant will incur all costs relating to infrastructure upgrades,
                   including offsite works, required to manage the subject property's drainage
                   concern, as a condition for rezoning the land;
            iv.    That the applicant agrees to submit a construction parking management plan,
                   subject to the approval of the Director of Engineering, prior to building permit
                   issuance;
             v.    That the applicant agrees to construct the building in substantial conformance
                   with Appendices "A" to "C";
            vi.    That applicant agrees to register, on title, a reciprocal agreement between the
                   two properties that grants each property access to, waste and recycling facilities,
                   bicycle stalls and all storage and building maintenance rooms.

       e) That the applicant registers, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a road dedication plan to the
           satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

3. Authorize the Director of Planning to issue the following variances through a Development
    Variance or Development Permit:

       a) A variance to Section 4.01.01 to reduce the required amount of bicycle parking for
          Building "A" from the required 78 to 0 on the condition that:
                 The applicant enter into an easement agreement in favor of the municipality, that
                 allows the bicycle parking required by Building "A" be provided on the parcel
                 occupied by Building "B;"
       b) A variance to Section 4.01.01 to reduce the required amount of required parking for an
          apartment within the City Centre from the required 45 resident parking stalls and 5 visitor
          parking stalls to 30 resident parking stalls and no visitor stalls, on the condition that:
                 The applicant enter into an easement agreement in favor of the municipality, that
                  allows the additional parking required by Building "B" be provided on the parcel
                  occupied by Building "A;"

candidates.raw_motion_text:
That Council:

   1.   Direct staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 3343,
        3347, and 3359 Luxton Road from RR2 (Rural Residential 2) to RS2 (Residential Small Lot 2) and
        RM2A (Attached Housing) subject to the following terms and conditions:

            a) •That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                contributions per one-family lot created, prior to subdivision approval:
                   i.   $3,960 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                  ii.   $660 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

            b) That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                contributions per townhouse unit, prior to building permit:
                   i.   $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                  ii.   $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

            c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
                 in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
                     i.   That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provide to the
                          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
                    ii.   That all municipal works and third party utility services are installed within
                          municipal road dedication;
                   iii.   That the west side of Piper Road include as many parking scallops as possible
                          within the size requirements of Bylaw 1000;
                   iv.    That a parks plan be developed for the dedicated open space along Piper Road to
                          the satisfaction of the Parks Manager prior to subdivision approval;
                    v.    That a storm water management plan be provided, which demonstrates the
                          required onsite detention, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
                   vi.    That notification be provided that the properties are close to agricultural
                          operations and the South Vancouver Rangers property, both of which may
                          generate nuisances;
                  vii.    That road dedication along Piper and Luxton Roads be provided to the satisfaction
                          of the Director of Engineering prior to subdivision approval.

   2. Direct staff to prepare a bylaw amendment to the RM2A (Attached Housing) Zone as per the
       following:

            b) By replacing 6.31A.05(1) with, "No building or structure may exceed a height of 3 storeys."

               3.0m; and
            c) That Section 6.36A.06(5) be varied to reduce the minimum rear yard setback to 5.0m.

That Development Variance Permit No. DVP17-0012 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford
to Seamus Brennan, TFIRMA Development Corp on behalf of 1106670 B.C. Ltd., Oakcrest Park Estates Ltd.,
Keycorp Industrial Developments Ltd., and Roberta Hilda Young to vary the Subdivision and Development
Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 requirements to waive the requirement for the proposed business park to connect
to the municipal sanitary sewer system and the CRD Water Distribution network and to permit them to install
Overhead Power within the subject properties 030-095-891, 030-095-883, 001-703-374; 2961, 2965, 3005 &
3021 Sooke Rd (Centre Mountain Properties) subject to the following terms and conditions:

1.   Variances


     The following regulations of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 are varied under
     Section 498 of the Local Government Act:


     a)   That Section 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to
          allow subdivision without connecting to the municipal sanitary sewer system, subject to the
          following conditions:

          That a covenant containing the following be registered on the title of the properties, to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering:

          i.   That the applicant design the on-site sewage disposal system to the approval of Island Health and
               to the satisfaction of the Chief Building Inspector prior to building permit; and

     b)   That Section 8.1 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to allow
          subdivision without water supply provided by the City or CRD Water Service, subject to the following
          conditions:

          That a covenant containing the following be registered on the title of the subject property, to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering:

          i.   That all buildings are to be connected to the City's, CRD Water, or an authorized third party
               distributer such as Sustainable Services Limited (SSL) water system within six (6) months of such

                                                                                                 September 17th, 2018
                                                                                                            Page 3 of 9


             service being extended along the frontage of the subject properties to the satisfaction of the
             Director of Engineering;
        ii. That the owner agrees to support any future petition to extend a Public Water Service system to
             the subject properties;
        iii. That installation of any on-site plumbing necessary to allow a Public Water Service system to be
             connected to each building in accordance with the BC Building Code and/or Subdivision and
             Servicing Bylaw No. 1000, is completed as part of the works and services installed on the subject
             properties;
        iv. That the owner prove that a well water supply for potable water is available and the proposed
             development meets the requirements of the City's Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw
             No. 1000 in respect of domestic water supply to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering
             prior to subdivision approval;
        v. That the owner demonstrate that the water wells to be used on site will not adversely affect the
             water supply available to the wells on surrounding properties prior to each subdivision of lands
             to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;
        vi. That each new building install a fire sprinkler system in accordance with the applicable NFPA
             standard, Building Bylaw No. 1160, and the current BC Building Code to the satisfaction of the
             Chief Building Inspector;
        vii. That a fire protection strategy be approved prior to each subdivision of the land to the
             satisfaction of the Fire Chief and Director of Engineering and be installed prior to the issuance of
             any Building Permits, including backup generators for any necessary pump systems;
        viii.That prior to issuance of each building permit the applicant provide a Fire Underwriters Survey
             or an approved alternative demonstrating the required fire flows are available to the satisfaction
             of the Langford Fire Chief; and
        ix. That the variance for water requirements, Section 8.1, is permitted to create up to 10 new lots
             not including the 7 existing lots and is valid for a maximum of 10 years from the date of issuance.
             No further subdivision approvals or building permits will be issued after this date unless an
             adequate City or CRD Water service is available;

AND


That Section 9.2 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to allow subdivision
without installing underground electrical and telecommunication.

Overhead Power within the subject properties 030-095-891, 030-095-883, 001-703-374; 2961, 2965, 3005 &
3021 Sooke Rd (Centre Mountain Properties) subject to the following terms and conditions:

1.   Variances


     The following regulations of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 are varied under
     Section 498 of the Local Government Act:


     a)   That Section 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to
          allow subdivision without connecting to the municipal sanitary sewer system, subject to the
          following conditions:

          That a covenant containing the following be registered on the title of the properties, to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering:

          i.   That the applicant design the on-site sewage disposal system to the approval of Island Health and
               to the satisfaction of the Chief Building Inspector prior to building permit; and

     b)   That Section 8.1 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to allow
          subdivision without water supply provided by the City or CRD Water Service, subject to the following
          conditions:

          That a covenant containing the following be registered on the title of the subject property, to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering:

          i.   That all buildings are to be connected to the City's, CRD Water, or an authorized third party
               distributer such as Sustainable Services Limited (SSL) water system within six (6) months of such

                                                                                                 September 17th, 2018
                                                                                                            Page 3 of 9


             service being extended along the frontage of the subject properties to the satisfaction of the
             Director of Engineering;
        ii. That the owner agrees to support any future petition to extend a Public Water Service system to
             the subject properties;
        iii. That installation of any on-site plumbing necessary to allow a Public Water Service system to be
             connected to each building in accordance with the BC Building Code and/or Subdivision and
             Servicing Bylaw No. 1000, is completed as part of the works and services installed on the subject
             properties;
        iv. That the owner prove that a well water supply for potable water is available and the proposed
             development meets the requirements of the City's Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw
             No. 1000 in respect of domestic water supply to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering
             prior to subdivision approval;
        v. That the owner demonstrate that the water wells to be used on site will not adversely affect the
             water supply available to the wells on surrounding properties prior to each subdivision of lands
             to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;
        vi. That each new building install a fire sprinkler system in accordance with the applicable NFPA
             standard, Building Bylaw No. 1160, and the current BC Building Code to the satisfaction of the
             Chief Building Inspector;
        vii. That a fire protection strategy be approved prior to each subdivision of the land to the
             satisfaction of the Fire Chief and Director of Engineering and be installed prior to the issuance of
             any Building Permits, including backup generators for any necessary pump systems;
        viii.That prior to issuance of each building permit the applicant provide a Fire Underwriters Survey
             or an approved alternative demonstrating the required fire flows are available to the satisfaction
             of the Langford Fire Chief; and
        ix. That the variance for water requirements, Section 8.1, is permitted to create up to 10 new lots
             not including the 7 existing lots and is valid for a maximum of 10 years from the date of issuance.
             No further subdivision approvals or building permits will be issued after this date unless an
             adequate City or CRD Water service is available;

AND


That Section 9.2 of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to allow subdivision
without installing underground electrical and telecommunication.

         Permit for Form and Character, to be located in the front or side yards for buildings located
         immediately next to the Galloping Goose.

That Council:


     1.   Direct staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 939
          Walfred from the RR5 (Rural Residential 5) to the RS3 (Residential Small Lot 3), and to amend the
          text within the RS3 zone for the subject property such that:


           a)        Secondary suites are permitted, in accordance with section 3.08, on all lots larger than 400 m 2
                     with a lot width greater than 12 m;
           b)        The total floor area of the of one family-dwelling on lots less than 400 m 2 may not exceed the
                     total area of the lots they occupy (e.g. 1.0 FSR);
           c)        The minimum lot size is reduced to 200


Subject to the following terms and conditions:


     2.   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus of increased density, the following contributions per
          new lot created, prior to subdivision approval:


                I.         $3,960 per lot towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
               II.         $660 per lot towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

                                                                                              February 4th, 2019
                                                                                                    Page 3 of 9


3.   That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

        I.   A technical memo from a qualified engineer that verifies storm water can adequately
             managed on-site, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
       II.   A site plan that shows the 9.5 land dedication, and 2.0 m wide proposed statutory right of
             way that will link the subject development to Walfred Road;

4.   That the applicant provides, prior to bylaw Adoption, a section 219 covenant, registered in priority
     overall all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

        I.   That the applicant agrees that all one-family dwellings with a secondary suite must include
             a double car driveway, provided that the width of the driveway does not exceed 50% of the
             width of the lot.
       II.   That the applicant complete full frontage improvements, including but not limited to:
             bicycle laning, off street parking, sidewalks, light standards and boulevard planting, in
             accordance with Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the Director of
             Engineering, prior to subdivision approval;
      III.   That the applicant construct, or provide a bond for, a 1.8m high solid board fence along the
             rear of lots that abut the 7.0 m wide dedicated open space adjacent to Walfred Road, prior
             to subdivision approval;
      IV.    That the applicant provide a construction parking management plan, to the satisfaction of
             the Director of Engineering, prior to issuance of a building permit;
       V.    That no driveway or other vehicle access will be created between the subject property and
             Walfred Road;

      VI.    That the applicant dedicate a 2.5 m wide area of land to accommodate frontage
             requirements, and off street parking along Walfred Road, as well as an additional 7.0 m
             wide dedicated area of land to the City between Walfred Road and the subject property,
             prior to subdivision approval;
     VII.    That the applicant provide a stormwater management plan, to the satisfaction of the
             Director of Engineering and in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000, prior to subdivision
             approval;
     VIII.   That the applicant agrees to implement the approved storm water management plan and
             to complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to on site and off site
             infrastructure necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject property at the
             applicant's expense;
      IX.    That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions
             or other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled at the applicant's expense;
       X.    That the applicant agrees to replant the 7.0 m wide dedicated area, to the satisfaction of
             the Director of Planning, contained within the tree retention plan for the adjacent property
             at 935 Walfred Road, prior to building permit issuance;
      XI.    That the applicant construct a 2.0 m wide pedestrian trail, linking the subject development
             to Walfred Road, prior to subdivision approval, which may be reduced to 1.0 m once the
             property to the west is developed;
     XII.    The applicant registers a statutory right of way for the construction of a pedestrian trail
             linking the proposed development to Walfred Road, prior to subdivision approval; and

                                                                                                          February 4th, 2019
                                                                                                                Page 4 of 9


        XIII.         The applicant registers a statutory right of way for a two-point turnaround, to the
                      satisfaction of the Fire Chief, registered in favour of the City, prior to subdivision approval;
        XIV.          The applicant registers a housing covenant for all lots less than 400 rn 2 that includes: a) no
                      more than two bathrooms and one two piece (powder room) permitted within each
                      dwelling, b) no more than one kitchen or food preparation area per dwelling, c) no separate
                      thermostat controls for separate parts of the single-family dwelling unit, and d) no
                      separation between floors or areas of the single-family dwelling unit.

                would include art work.

          i.    That a 2.0m wide pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road
                be constructed with red brick paves and lighting prior to issuance of a building
                permit, to the satisfaction of the Parks Manager; and
          ii.   That the southwest corner of the proposed commercial/residential site have a
                pedestrian plaza with art work installed prior to issuance of a building permit, to
                the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;

     to subdivision approval for the creation of more than one lot located north of the SPEA and more
     than one lot located south of the SPEA.


c)   That the applicant provides the following prior to Public Hearing:


         i.        A technical memorandum regarding proposed stormwater management for the
                   development, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

              i.   Construct full frontage improvements, in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000 standards and
